Sylvan & Scourge - Project Board

Updated Oct 10, 2026 · Submit to App Store Oct 26 · Live about Nov 2
How to use this board (2-minute read)

What each column means

  • Ideas - "maybe someday." Nobody is working on these. Parking them here keeps them from getting lost.
  • Backlog - real work we plan to do, just not this week. Includes things you've decided that aren't built yet.
  • Next Up (Sprint) - what we've committed to finish this sprint. Top card = most important.
  • In Development - someone is actively working on it right now.
  • Review / Waiting on Robert - finished work for you to check (usually on your phone), or a decision only you can make.
  • Done - finished, on the main build, and signed off by you.

Where this board comes from

Every card here is a card on the project's master board (the small SS number on each card). This page is rebuilt from it, so it can't drift: when a card moves on the master board, it moves here the next time the page is rebuilt.

What a sprint is

A sprint is a short, fixed block of time (here: one week, Thursday to Wednesday) with a small list of work we promise to finish. If something doesn't fit, it goes back to Backlog instead of quietly slipping.

Current sprint: Sprint 2, Oct 8-14. Goal: battles switched on for the beta (you said yes, 10/9), the store-build switches in, the privacy page live, and the Oct 11 beta build out. **Beta date (Fable, confirmed 10/9): beta build Oct 11, outside testers Oct 12 - ON TRACK: the beta build (196) was green on Oct 9; only the tester group (SS-425, Robert) remains.**

How to move cards

Tap ◀ or ▶ on a card to move it on this device only. To make a move permanent, tell Claude ("move SS-414 to Done" or "answer to SS-415: research") and the board is rebuilt.

Suggested weekly routine (about 15 minutes)

  • Wednesday evening - review: look at Review / Waiting on Robert. Answer the top 2-3 (one line each is enough).
  • Thursday - plan the sprint: pick the next few cards from Backlog into Next Up. No more than 6-8 cards.
  • End of each sprint: are we still on track for the submit date? If not, cut scope, not quality.

Who's who

Robert decides, tests on the phone, runs the Mac and App Store steps. Claude writes code, specs and docs. Grok makes the art.

This board holds topics only - no code and nothing private. It is rebuilt from the project's master board; the SS number on each card is its card there.
